body:
## Module 2 in two minutes

**Your job is described as one role and it is three**, sorted by what happens if you get it wrong. **Fiduciary and governance** — a legal or fiduciary consequence with your name on it. **The operating system** — the function stops working. **Strategic counsel** — the company makes a worse decision, and nobody ever knows.

**AI compresses the middle and expands both ends** `[V]`. The operating system is transactional, high-volume and rule-governed, which is the profile automation has found in every function it has touched — and it is the largest budget line in most People functions. **Governance expands**, and you acquire it through other people's procurement decisions, which is a new way to acquire an obligation.

**Strategic counsel expands too, and the mechanism matters.** It was never limited by intelligence. It was limited by **the cost of knowing things** — which exit interviews you had read, whether you could compare this restructure against the last four. That cost collapsed.

## The through-line

**The scarce resource moved from information to nerve.**

*"We don't have the data"* was doing enormous work in this function — true most of the time, and also **shelter.** It excused the recommendation you didn't make and the peer you didn't contradict. What's left, when you can know the thing, is whether you'll say it. That was always the actual job; the information constraint concealed how much of it was courage.

## What the full module adds

The two boundary cases that make the sorting real — the reorganization, where designing the structure and telling the CEO it won't survive the two directors are the *same meeting in different tiers*, and the AI policy, where writing it is operating system and refusing a peer's exception is governance. The three readings of a calendar-versus-budget disagreement and what each predicts. Twelve entries to sort. And the activity: both numbers, rough, plus **one thing you would move and what it comes out of** — because an addition without a subtraction is not a decision at this altitude.
